newsitem.title: USA: AMR says pilot dispute threatens company.
newsitem.headline: AMR says pilot dispute threatens company.

text.p: The labour dispute with pilots at American Airlines has left the company's management fearing for the future of the carrier, a top executive said Wednesday.

Gerard Arpey, chief financial officer of American Airlines parent AMR Corp., said, "We, quite frankly, are at a loss as to what to do next: accept a contract that would be at best uncompetitive vs. our principal competitors, or a possible cessation of operations. Two disastrous sort of alternatives."

In a conference call with reporters, Arpey said he had been at the Fort Worth, Texas-based company for 15 years and that the current labour dispute was "as grave a situation as I've seen the company face in my career here."

Arpey said pilots had shown no sign of accepting binding arbitration in the dispute and said he expects the National Mediation Board to order both sides into a 30-day "cooling off" period in their contract dispute as early as Wednesday night.
If no agreement is reached in the 30-day period, the union would be free to strike, while the carrier could implement new work conditions or simply lock out its pilots.
Both sides have agreed that the outcome of such an all-out confrontation would define the airline's future.
Arpey said he hoped mediators would be able to broker an agreement.

He said the pilots' latest proposal would leave American at a cost disadvantage of "hundreds of millions of dollars" against its main competitors, UAL Corp.'s United Airlines and Delta Air Lines Inc., in the years ahead.
